BOF = basic oxygen furnace; HDG = hot-dip galvanization 4.3.1 Technology Trends for Torque Tubes Torque tubes come in various shapes, which represent a balance between ease of manufacturing, material use, structural integrity, and integration into specific tracker systems (Medium 2024). For example, Nextracker uses round tubes, Array Technologies uses octagonal tubes, and GameChange Solar uses square tubes (Array Technologies 2020; GameChange Solar 2025; Nextracker 2019; Unimacts 2025). These torque tubes are typically made of steel and are galvanized to protect them from corrosion (National Material Company 2023). The specifications of torque tubes—such as length, diameter, wall thickness, and steel grade— are important to assess U.S. manufacturing readiness. Typical round torque tubes are 114–165 mm in diameter, with wall thicknesses of 2.5–5 mm, and weights of 6–16 kg/m, depending on geometry and steel grade (PandaPipe 2025; Nextracker 2020; TUS Pipe 2022). These dimensions fall within the production capabilities of domestic roll-forming and tube mill facilities, which are designed to handle common structural steel sections. This contrasts with 75 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. other renewable sectors such as offshore wind, where monopiles and flanges often exceed U.S. forging and forming capabilities. Torque tube specifications used in PV system installations are not niche or exotic, and they are often standard sizes readily produced using hot-rolled steel coils and inline galvanization— processes widely available in the U.S. steel sector. In fact, leading suppliers, such as Unimacts and Attala Steel, manufacture torque tubes domestically using locally sourced steel (Attala Steel 2025; Unimacts 2025). This suggests that most torque tubes used in utility-scale PV systems are both manufacturable and procurable domestically, aligning with 45X and ITC domestic content compliance. 4.3.2 Domestic Production of Torque Tubes The data needed to estimate total U.S. torque tube manufacturing capacity are not publicly available. However, industry announcements and manufacturing partnerships suggest the equivalent of multiple gigawatts of torque tubes were domestically produced in the United States in 2024, with additional production capacity planned. Domestic torque tube manufacturers include Lock Joint Tube, Atkore, OMCO, BCI Steel, JM Steel, MSS Steel Tubes, Priefert Steel, Nucor, Unimacts, and Zekelman Industries. Many of these companies have partnered with leading solar tracker companies, including Array Technologies, GameChange Solar, and Nextracker (U.S. Department of Energy 2025c; Zekelman Industries 2025). 4.3.3 Imports/Exports of Torque Tubes Torque tubes have a low value-to-weight ratio, making imports less competitive because of high transport costs.
